content: As a boy, Samuel served the LORD under which priest?
explanation: Samuel grew up in the house of the LORD. “And the boy Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli.” (1 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: When the LORD first called young Samuel at night, what did Samuel answer?
explanation: Samuel was ready to listen. “Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, “Here I am.”” (1 Samuel 3:4, BSB)

content: When young Samuel heard his name called at night, who did he think was calling?
explanation: He did not yet know the LORD's voice. “He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you have called me.”” (1 Samuel 3:5, BSB)

content: How many times did the LORD call young Samuel before Eli realized it was God?
explanation: Then Eli knew the LORD was calling the boy. “Once again, for the third time, the LORD called to Samuel.” (1 Samuel 3:8, BSB)

content: What did Eli tell young Samuel to say if God called him again?
options: Speak, LORD, Your servant is listening
explanation: Samuel learned to listen to God. “Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.” (1 Samuel 3:9, BSB)

content: Where was young Samuel lying down when God called him?
options: In the temple of the LORD
explanation: The ark of God was there. “Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was located.” (1 Samuel 3:3, BSB)

content: As Samuel grew up, what did all Israel come to know about him?
explanation: The LORD was with Samuel. “knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.” (1 Samuel 3:20, BSB)

content: After God rejected King Saul, to whose family did He send Samuel to find a new king?
explanation: God had chosen a king from Jesse's sons. “I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem” (1 Samuel 16:1, BSB)

content: When Samuel was impressed by Jesse's tall son, what did God say He looks at?
explanation: People judge by looks, but God sees inside. “For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7, BSB)

content: How many of Jesse's sons passed before Samuel without being chosen?
explanation: The LORD had not chosen any of them. “Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel” (1 Samuel 16:10, BSB)

content: When Samuel came to anoint a new king, where was Jesse's youngest son?
explanation: No one thought the youngest would be chosen. ““There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.”” (1 Samuel 16:11, BSB)

content: What did Samuel use to anoint young David?
explanation: He anointed David in front of his brothers. “So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers” (1 Samuel 16:13, BSB)

content: After Samuel anointed David, what came upon him?
explanation: From that day God's Spirit was with David. “and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.” (1 Samuel 16:13, BSB)

content: When King Saul was troubled, what instrument did young David play for him?
explanation: Saul felt better when David played. “David would pick up his harp and play” (1 Samuel 16:23, BSB)

content: Which Philistine champion challenged the army of Israel?
explanation: He was a giant warrior from Gath. “Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp.” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: When Goliath shouted his challenge, how did Saul and the Israelites feel?
explanation: No one wanted to fight the giant. “Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.” (1 Samuel 17:11, BSB)

content: Before facing Goliath, which wild animals did David say he had fought while keeping sheep?
explanation: God had already helped David against them. “and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock” (1 Samuel 17:34, BSB)

content: Why did David take off King Saul's armor before facing Goliath?
options: He was not used to it
explanation: David trusted God, not armor. “I am not accustomed to them.” (1 Samuel 17:39, BSB)

content: How many smooth stones did David choose from the brook before facing Goliath?
explanation: He put them in his shepherd's bag. “selected five smooth stones from the brook” (1 Samuel 17:40, BSB)

content: Facing Goliath, in whose name did David say he came?
explanation: Goliath had defied the living God. “but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts” (1 Samuel 17:45, BSB)

content: Where did David's stone hit Goliath?
explanation: The giant fell facedown. “striking the Philistine on the forehead.” (1 Samuel 17:49, BSB)

content: With what did young David defeat Goliath?
explanation: God gave the victory without a sword in David's hand. “Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone” (1 Samuel 17:50, BSB)

content: After David defeated Goliath, whose soul became knit together with David's?
explanation: Jonathan, Saul's son, loved David as himself. “the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together” (1 Samuel 18:1, BSB)

content: Why did Jonathan make a covenant with David?
explanation: They became best friends. “Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.” (1 Samuel 18:3, BSB)

content: What did Jonathan give David as a sign of their friendship?
explanation: He also gave David his tunic and belt. “And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.” (1 Samuel 18:4, BSB)

content: What song of the women made King Saul jealous of David?
options: Saul his thousands, David tens of thousands
explanation: Saul was angry that David got more praise. “Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.” (1 Samuel 18:7, BSB)

content: In his jealousy, what did King Saul throw at David?
explanation: David escaped that night. “Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear.” (1 Samuel 19:10, BSB)

content: To send David a secret warning, what did Jonathan plan to shoot?
explanation: Where the arrows landed would tell David what to do. “I will shoot three arrows to the side of it” (1 Samuel 20:20, BSB)

content: When David and Jonathan said goodbye, what did they do?
explanation: David had to flee from Saul. “Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together” (1 Samuel 20:41, BSB)

content: When King Saul hunted David with three thousand men, where was David?
explanation: Saul was told where David was hiding. “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.” (1 Samuel 24:1, BSB)

content: When Saul stepped into a cave at En-gedi, who was hiding deep inside?
explanation: Saul did not know they were there. “And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.” (1 Samuel 24:3, BSB)

content: In the cave at En-gedi, what did David secretly cut off?
explanation: David could have killed Saul, but he did not. “Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.” (1 Samuel 24:4, BSB)

content: Why would David not harm King Saul in the cave?
explanation: David left Saul's fate to God. “May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.” (1 Samuel 24:6, BSB)

content: How did David feel after cutting the corner of Saul's robe?
explanation: Even that small act felt wrong to him. “Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken” (1 Samuel 24:5, BSB)

content: After David spared his life, what did King Saul say to him?
options: You are more righteous than I
explanation: David had repaid evil with good. “You are more righteous than I” (1 Samuel 24:17, BSB)

content: When Saul heard David calling to him outside the cave, what did Saul do?
explanation: Saul was moved by David's mercy. “Then Saul wept aloud” (1 Samuel 24:16, BSB)

content: Who were the two wives of Elkanah, Samuel's father?
explanation: Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none. “He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah.” (1 Samuel 1:2, BSB)

content: What did Hannah promise God if He gave her a son?
options: To give a lamb every year
To dedicate him to the LORD
explanation: She kept her promise. “then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life” (1 Samuel 1:11, BSB)

content: Why did Hannah name her son Samuel?
options: He was born in the temple
She asked the LORD for him
explanation: God answered her prayer. “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.” (1 Samuel 1:20, BSB)

content: When Samuel was a boy, how often did the word of the LORD come?
explanation: Visions were scarce in those days. “Now in those days the word of the LORD was rare and visions were scarce.” (1 Samuel 3:1, BSB)

content: When the Philistines captured the ark of God, which of Eli's sons died?
explanation: It was a dark day for Israel. “The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.” (1 Samuel 4:11, BSB)

content: When Samuel was old, what did the people of Israel ask him to give them?
explanation: They wanted to be like other nations. “Now appoint a king to judge us like all the other nations.” (1 Samuel 8:5, BSB)

content: When Israel asked Samuel for a king, whom did God say they had really rejected?
explanation: God was meant to be their king. “For it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected Me as their king.” (1 Samuel 8:7, BSB)

content: How is Saul described before he became Israel's first king?
explanation: He was choice and handsome. “a head taller than any of the people.” (1 Samuel 9:2, BSB)

content: When Samuel presented Saul to Israel as king, what did the people shout?
explanation: Saul became Israel's first king. “And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”” (1 Samuel 10:24, BSB)

content: When Saul disobeyed, Samuel said the LORD had found a man after what?
explanation: That man would be David. “the LORD has sought a man after His own heart” (1 Samuel 13:14, BSB)

content: Samuel told disobedient King Saul that what is better than sacrifice?
explanation: God wants His people to listen and obey. “Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice” (1 Samuel 15:22, BSB)

content: Which of Jesse's sons did Samuel first think was God's chosen king?
explanation: Samuel judged by appearance at first. “When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab” (1 Samuel 16:6, BSB)

content: How is young David described when he was brought in from the sheep?
explanation: The LORD said, “He is the one.” “He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance.” (1 Samuel 16:12, BSB)

content: Goliath the giant came from which Philistine city?
explanation: He was the Philistines' champion. “Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: Before the battle with Goliath, what did David go back and forth to do?
explanation: He was still a shepherd in Bethlehem. “but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.” (1 Samuel 17:15, BSB)

content: Why did Saul first say David could not fight Goliath?
explanation: Goliath had been a warrior from his youth. “You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.” (1 Samuel 17:33, BSB)

content: David told Goliath that God does not save by sword or spear, because the battle belongs to whom?
explanation: David trusted God to win. “for the battle is the LORD’s” (1 Samuel 17:47, BSB)

content: After Goliath fell, what did the Philistine army do?
explanation: Their hero was dead. “When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.” (1 Samuel 17:51, BSB)

content: Which of King Saul's daughters did David marry?
explanation: Saul gave her to David as his wife. “Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.” (1 Samuel 18:27, BSB)

content: After the women's song about David, how did King Saul treat him?
options: Kept a jealous eye on him
explanation: Saul feared David would take the kingdom. “And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.” (1 Samuel 18:9, BSB)

content: While running from Saul, where did David take refuge after leaving Gath?
explanation: His family came to him there. “So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam.” (1 Samuel 22:1, BSB)

content: Who was the wise wife of harsh Nabal?
explanation: She was intelligent and beautiful. “His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail.” (1 Samuel 25:3, BSB)

content: Before his last battle, whom did King Saul seek out at Endor?
explanation: Saul had turned away from the LORD. “There is a medium at Endor” (1 Samuel 28:7, BSB)

content: How did King Saul die in battle with the Philistines?
options: He fell on his own sword
explanation: His armor-bearer was too afraid to kill him. “So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.” (1 Samuel 31:4, BSB)

content: Elkanah, Samuel's father, came from which town?
explanation: It was in the hill country of Ephraim. “Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim” (1 Samuel 1:1, BSB)

content: Hannah promised that her son would never have what come over his head?
explanation: He would be set apart for God all his life. “and no razor shall ever come over his head.” (1 Samuel 1:11, BSB)

content: When God called young Samuel, what was wrong with old Eli?
explanation: Eli could not see. “Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see” (1 Samuel 3:2, BSB)

content: Samuel was known as a true prophet across Israel from where to where?
explanation: This meant the whole land. “So all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew” (1 Samuel 3:20, BSB)

content: Which son of Jesse was presented to Samuel right after Abinadab?
explanation: The LORD had not chosen him either. “Next Jesse presented Shammah” (1 Samuel 16:9, BSB)

content: How tall was Goliath?
explanation: That is about nine and a half feet. “He was six cubits and a span in height” (1 Samuel 17:4, BSB)

content: How much did the iron point of Goliath's spear weigh?
explanation: His spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. “and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels.” (1 Samuel 17:7, BSB)

content: What was Goliath's coat of mail made of?
explanation: It weighed five thousand shekels. “He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels” (1 Samuel 17:5, BSB)

content: How many Philistines did David and his men kill to become Saul's son-in-law?
explanation: Then Saul gave him Michal. “David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines.” (1 Samuel 18:27, BSB)

content: In Jonathan's arrow signal, which words meant David had to flee?
options: The arrows are on this side
explanation: It meant the LORD was sending David away. “Look, the arrows are beyond you” (1 Samuel 20:22, BSB)

content: How many chosen men did Saul take to hunt David near En-gedi?
explanation: They searched the rocky hills. “So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel” (1 Samuel 24:2, BSB)

content: In which rocky region did Saul look for David near En-gedi?
options: The Rocks of the Wild Goats
explanation: David was hiding in the caves there. “in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.” (1 Samuel 24:2, BSB)

content: Nabal, Abigail's harsh husband, belonged to which clan?
explanation: He was evil in his dealings. “but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.” (1 Samuel 25:3, BSB)
